dial.summary: Risk Off persists following the FOMC's September 16 hike (+25bps to 3.75%–4.00%, first since 2023) and hawkish dot plot removing all 2027 cuts, which drove DXY above 100 into headwind territory for the first time since July, pushed the 10Y nominal to 5.016%, and sent TOTAL crypto down to $2.67T from $2.75T; with real yields at 2.57%+ and the 2s10s curve flattening sharply from +41bps to +28bps post-FOMC, BTC.D easing to 57.0% from 59.2% in a broad sell-off, no conditions for accumulation or rotation have materialized.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at $103.5T as of September 2026 (MacroMicro/SpendNode latest G4 estimate); up from ~$103.4T four weeks prior (August 2026 estimate); 4-week trend up confirmed (sustained upward direction); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); broader global M2 (all major central banks) reached a record ~$150T in June 2026 per SpendNode/MacroMicro; synchronized global tightening (Fed Sep 16 +25bps, BOE Sep 17 hold at 3.75%, BOJ Sep 18 decision pending at 88% hike probability) will apply modest G4 M2 headwinds through Q4 2026; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; next ISM Manufacturing release October 1, 2026 (September data); status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); FOMC Sep 16 hike to 3.75%–4.00% with hawkish dot plot removing 2027 cuts adds financing-cost pressure to manufacturing capex; S&P Global Flash PMI Sep 23 is the next advance manufacturing read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 100.07 on September 17, 2026 — crossed above the 100 headwind threshold for the first time since July, driven by the FOMC Sep 16 hike (+25bps to 3.75%–4.00%, first since 2023) and a hawkish dot plot removing all previously expected 2027 rate cuts; 4-week trend up: ~99.60 (Aug 14) → 100.07 (Sep 17) = +0.47%; status headwind (ICE DXY above 100 per rules); RSI overbought at 83.54 post-FOMC; BOE held at 3.75% Sep 17 (6-3 split) with minimal DXY impact; BOJ Sep 18 hike (88% probability, expected +25bps to 1.25%) remains the primary DXY downside risk via yen carry-trade unwind; every major currency weakened against the dollar post-FOMC.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 last confirmed at 2.57% as of September 14, 2026 (pre-FOMC; Sep 14 is latest FRED H.15 value available); FOMC Sep 16 hike drove 10Y nominal from ~4.80% to 5.016% (+22bps) while breakevens remained anchored near 2.33% — post-FOMC DFII10 likely higher (estimated 2.68–2.73%) pending FRED H.15 Sep 16 publication; Sep 14 value carried forward as last confirmed read; 4-week trend up: ~2.39% (Aug 11) → 2.57% (Sep 14) = +18bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); sustained extreme real yield headwind continues to weigh on duration-sensitive risk assets.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: Post-FOMC (Sep 16, 2026) close: 10Y 5.016%, 2Y 4.738%, spread = +0.28% (+28bps); 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+35bps (Aug 12) → +28bps (Sep 16) = −7bps; 2Y front-end repriced +34bps on the hawkish dot plot removing 2027 cuts, outpacing the 10Y's +22bps rise; curve flattened sharply from +41bps (Sep 15) to +28bps in a single post-FOMC session; status neutral (positive spread but NOT steepening — supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening); curve remains structurally positive following uninversion in 2026; BOJ Sep 18 hike could steepen the curve if long-end responds to global rate repricing.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T for week ending September 9, 2026 (H.4.1 released September 11, confirmed $6,740,619M); new H.4.1 for week ending September 16 released today (Sep 17 at 4:30 PM ET) — Sep 9 value carried forward pending indexing; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.74T (Sep 9) = +$40B, within flat threshold; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT with no acceleration; FOMC Sep 16 decision did not announce any change to balance sheet normalization pace); composition: $4,552B Treasuries, $1,914B MBS, $275B other.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.01% per 8h (MacroMicro Sep 9 confirmed; Coinglass direct fetch unavailable); 30-day trend flat: near-zero throughout August–September 2026; status supportive (near-zero confirms spot-driven price action, not leveraged-long crowding; well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); BTC.D fell from 59.2% to 57.0% post-FOMC (Sep 17) as TOTAL declined from $2.75T to $2.67T in a broad risk-off sell-off; near-zero funding amid the sell-off confirms orderly spot-driven deleveraging rather than forced liquidations; funding will be confirmed when Coinglass is accessible.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$306B (September 17, 2026; CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap); total crypto market cap $2.67T (down from $2.75T, post-FOMC risk-off); stablecoin dominance 11.5% ($306B / $2.67T); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 → 11.5% (Sep 17) = ~2pp decline over 30 days confirming net capital deployment into risk assets on the 30-day lens; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply as TOTAL fell from $2.75T → $2.67T); USDT leads at $183.4B (60.6% share), USDC $74.2B; BTC.D at 57.0% (eased from 59.2%).

upcoming.title: Bank of Japan Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting Sep 17–18, with Statement on Monetary Policy expected Sep 18 (midday Tokyo / ~3:30 AM ET); 88% market-implied hike probability; expected +25bps to 1.25%, highest since 1993; a hike would strengthen JPY and risk yen carry-trade unwinds with broad impact on global risk assets including crypto; DXY at 100.07 (headwind) — a hawkish BOJ could accelerate dollar weakness back toward the 97.5 supportive threshold; Japan core inflation ~2.5–2.8%, above BOJ's 2% target; BOJ decision follows FOMC +25bps (Sep 16) and BOE hold (Sep 17) completing the central bank triple-header.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization for August 2026 at 9:15 AM ET — measures output of manufacturing, mining, and utilities; released same day as BOJ decision; a strong reading reinforces ISM Manufacturing's expansion signal (54.6 in August); capacity utilization approaching 80% would add to inflationary pressures; watch energy sector output given elevated PPI energy components.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: S&P Global US Flash PMI Composite, Manufacturing, and Services preliminary data for September 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first advance look at September activity capturing full post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ reaction; leads ISM Manufacturing (Oct 1) and ISM Services (Oct 5); a sub-50 manufacturing reading would materially alter November FOMC rate-path narrative; DXY above 100 and 10Y yields at 5%+ provide a challenging backdrop for new business activity; August 2026 S&P Global Manufacturing PMI showed expansion with growth slipping to a 3-month low.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 20, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 20, 2026 — second labor market read post-FOMC Sep 16; will reflect whether the Fed/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster has any near-term impact on hiring decisions; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks and could shift October 27–28 FOMC expectations.
